name: Avg
description: Returns the average (arithmetic mean) of the values in the group.

examples.query: SELECT avg(SWISColumn) as ResultColumn FROM SWISTable

name: Count
description: Returns the number of non-NULL values in the group.

examples.query: SELECT count(SWISColumn) as ResultColumn FROM SWISTable

name: Max
description: Returns the largest value in the group.

examples.query: SELECT max(SWISColumn) as ResultColumn FROM SWISTable

name: Min
description: Returns the smallest value in the group.

examples.query: SELECT min(SWISColumn) as ResultColumn FROM SWISTable

name: String_Agg
description: Concatenates the non-NULL string values in the group into a single string, separated by separator. Both expression and separator are required. An optional ordering expression controls the order in which values are concatenated; its direction is optional and defaults to ascending. Returns NULL when the group has no non-NULL values.

name: Sum
description: Returns the arithmetic sum of the values in the group.

examples.query: SELECT sum(SWISColumn) as ResultColumn FROM SWISTable

name: ArrayContains
description: Returns true if array a contains value v.

name: ArrayLength
description: Returns the number of elements in array a.

examples.query: SELECT ArrayLength(MemberAncestorDetailsUrls) AS ColumnResult FROM Orion.ContainerMembers
examples.notes: in case array is NULL -> it returns NULL

name: ArrayValueAt
description: Returns the array element at position i in array a, counting from zero.

examples.query: SELECT ArrayValueAt(MemberAncestorDetailsUrls,0) AS ColumnResult FROM Orion.ContainerMembers
examples.notes: in case array is NULL -> it returns NULL,index starts with 0, in case index is out of range -> query fails

name: SplitStringToArray
description: Splits string a on comma separators into an array of substrings.

examples.query: SELECT SplitStringToArray('Hello|§|§|world') as a FROM Orion.Engines

name: ChangeTimeZone
description: The second argument needs to follow the standard timezone offset +/-hh:mm . The date in the database will have its offset changed to the specified timezone offset. The + must be within the ' '

examples.query: SELECT ChangeTimeZone(KeepAlive,'+05:00') as ColumnResult FROM Orion.Engines
examples.notes: The second argument needs to follow the standard timezone offset +/-hh:mm . The date in the database will have its offset changed to the specified timezone offset. The + must be within the ' '

name: AddDate
description: Returns a date n units after d, where the unit is specified by the first parameter u, which must be one of: 'millisecond', 'second', 'minute', 'hour', 'day', 'week', 'month', or 'year'. The u argument must be a string literal. It can't be a query parameter or value derived from the data.

examples.query: SELECT AddDate('month', 2, KeepAlive) AS ColumnResult From Orion.Engines
examples.notes: Add time to current Date Supported values for DatePart Millisecond, Second, Minute, Hour, Week, Day, Month, Year

name: AddDay
description: Returns a date n days after d.

examples.query: SELECT AddDay(17, KeepAlive) AS ColumnResult From Orion.Engines

name: AddHour
description: Returns a date n hours after d.

examples.query: SELECT Addhour(1, KeepAlive) AS ColumnResult From Orion.Engines

name: AddMillisecond
description: Returns a date n milliseconds after d.

examples.query: SELECT AddMillisecond(1, NextPoll) AS NextPoll From Orion.Nodes

name: AddMinute
description: Returns a date n minutes after d.

examples.query: SELECT Addminute(30, KeepAlive) AS ColumnResult From Orion.Engines

name: AddMonth
description: Returns a date n months after d.

examples.query: SELECT AddMonth(5, KeepAlive) AS ColumnResult From Orion.Engines

name: AddSecond
description: Returns a date n seconds after d.

examples.query: SELECT AddSecond(13, KeepAlive) AS ColumnResult From Orion.Engines

name: AddWeek
description: Returns a date n weeks after d.

examples.query: SELECT AddWeek(7, KeepAlive) AS ColumnResult From Orion.Engines

name: AddYear
description: Returns a date n years after d.

examples.query: SELECT AddYear(5, KeepAlive) AS ColumnResult From Orion.Engines

name: DateTime
description: Converts a string to a date. In most scenarios this conversion will happen automatically when needed by usage.

examples.query: SELECT KeepAlive FROM Orion.Engines where KeepAlive > DateTime('9/25/2015 3:49:54')
examples.notes: Time derived from SQL Server time zone settings

name: DateTrunc
description: Where 'datepart' is one of the following strings: 'minute', 'hour', 'day', 'week', 'month', 'quarter', 'year'. Returns a date like d, but with all components more granular than 'datepart' set to zero.

examples.query: SELECT DateTrunc('month', KeepAlive) as ColumnResult FROM Orion.Engines
examples.notes: Supported values for the DatePart argument: Minute, Hour, Week, Day, DayOfYear, Month, Quarter, Year. Not supported: Millisecond, Second.

name: Day
description: Returns the day of the month of d.

examples.query: SELECT Day(KeepAlive) as ColumnResult from orion.engines

name: DayDiff
description: Returns the number of days (rounded to the nearest integer) that b is later than a.

examples.query: SELECT DayDiff(KeepAlive,KeepAlive+28) as ColumnResult from orion.engines
examples.notes: +28 is the number of days difference from the Keepalive Column

name: DayOfYear
description: Returns the day of year of d. January 1 is 1, February 1 is 32, etc.

examples.query: SELECT DayofYear(KeepAlive) as ColumnResult from orion.engines

name: Downsample
description: Rounds the supplied timestamp d to the defined time period p.  For example, a period of '00:15:00' would round to the nearest 15 minute time increment. Requires Orion 2018.3 or later.

name: GetDate
description: Returns the current date in local time at the Orion server.

examples.query: SELECT getdate() as ResultCoumn FROM Orion.Engines
examples.notes: Time derived from SQL Server time zone settings

name: GetUtcDate
description: Returns the current date and time in UTC. Please note [possible issues](possible-issues/#datetime-functions).

examples.query: SELECT GetUtcDate() as ResultColumn FROM Orion.Engines
examples.notes: Time derived from SQL Server time zone settings

name: Hour
description: Returns the hour part of d (in 24 hour format).

examples.query: SELECT Hour(KeepAlive) as ColumnResult from orion.engines

name: HourDiff
description: Returns the number of hours (rounded to the nearest integer) that b is later than a.

examples.query: SELECT HourDiff(KeepAlive,KeepAlive+28) as ColumnResult from orion.engines
examples.notes: +28 is the number of days difference from the Keepalive Column

name: Millisecond
description: Returns the millisecond part of d.

examples.query: SELECT MilliSecond(KeepAlive) as ColumnResult from orion.engines

name: MillisecondDiff
description: Returns the number of milliseconds (rounded to the nearest integer) that b is later than a.

examples.query: SELECT MillisecondDiff(KeepAlive,KeepAlive+24) as ColumnResult from orion.engines
examples.notes: 24 is the number of days. 24 is also the max that can used for this query

name: Minute
description: Returns the minute part of d.

examples.query: SELECT Minute(KeepAlive) as ColumnResult from orion.engines

name: MinuteDiff
description: Returns the number of minutes (rounded to the nearest integer) that b is later than a.

examples.query: SELECT MinuteDiff(KeepAlive,KeepAlive+28) as ColumnResult from orion.engines
examples.notes: +28 is the number of days difference from the Keepalive Column

name: Month
description: Returns the month part of d. January is 1.

examples.query: SELECT Month(KeepAlive) as ColumnResult from orion.engines

name: MonthDiff
description: Returns the number of months (rounded to the nearest integer) that b is later than a.

examples.query: SELECT MonthDiff(KeepAlive,KeepAlive+28) as ColumnResult from orion.engines
examples.notes: +28 is the number of days difference from the Keepalive Column

name: QuarterOfYear
description: Returns the quarter of the year that contains d. January, February, and March are 1; April, May, and June are 2; etc.

examples.query: SELECT QuarterofYear(KeepAlive) as ColumnResult from orion.engines

name: Second
description: Returns the second part of d.

examples.query: SELECT Second(KeepAlive) as ColumnResult from orion.engines

name: SecondDiff
description: Returns the number of seconds (rounded to the nearest integer) that b is later than a.

examples.query: SELECT SecondDiff(KeepAlive, KeepAlive + 1) as a FROM Orion.Engines
examples.notes: +28 is the number of days difference from the Keepalive Column

name: ToLocal
description: Converts d to local time on the Orion server.

examples.query: SELECT Tolocal(getutcdate()) as ResultColumn FROM Orion.Engines
examples.notes: Time derived from SQL Server time zone settings

name: ToUtc
description: Converts d to UTC time.

examples.query: SELECT ToUtc(getdate()) as ResultColumn FROM Orion.Engines
examples.notes: Time derived from SQL Server time zone settings

name: Week
description: Returns the week number of d.

examples.query: SELECT Week(KeepAlive) as ColumnResult from orion.engines

name: WeekDay
description: Returns the day of the week of d as a number, with Sunday = 0, Monday = 1, ..., Saturday = 6. Available in Orion Platform 2016.1 and later.

examples.query: SELECT WeekDay(KeepAlive) as ColumnResult from orion.engines

name: WeekDiff
description: Returns the number of weeks (rounded to the nearest integer) that b is later than a.

examples.query: SELECT WeekDiff(KeepAlive,KeepAlive+28) as ColumnResult from orion.engines
examples.notes: +28 is the number of days difference from the Keepalive Column

name: Year
description: Returns the year of d.

examples.query: SELECT Year(KeepAlive) as ColumnResult from orion.engines

name: YearDiff
description: Returns the number of years (rounded to the nearest integer) that b is later than a.

examples.query: SELECT YearDiff(KeepAlive,'1/01/2020 0:0:0 AM') as ColumnResult from orion.engines

name: Case
signature: Case when c then a else b end
description: Returns a if c is true else returns b.

name: IsNull
description: Returns a unless it is NULL, else returns b.

examples.query: SELECT Restart, IsNull(restart, '9/25/2015 3:49:54') as ColumnResult FROM Orion.Engines

name: UNION
description: Adds the results of an additional query q directly below the former, the number of columns must match between unioned queries

name: Abs
description: Returns the absolute value of n.

examples.query: SELECT abs(-1) as ResultColumn FROM SWISTable

name: Ceiling
description: Returns the smallest integer that is not less than n.

examples.query: SELECT ceiling(ResponseTime) as ResultColumn FROM Orion.Nodes
examples.notes: The Ceiling() will rounded up any positive or negative decimal value within the function upwards.

name: Floor
description: Returns the largest integer that is not greater than n.

examples.query: SELECT floor(ResponseTime) as ResultColumn FROM Orion.Nodes
examples.notes: The FLOOR() rounded up any positive or negative decimal value down to the next least integer value.

name: Round
description: Returns n rounded to the p decimal places.

examples.query: SELECT round(ResponseTime, PercentLoss) as ResultColumn FROM Orion.Nodes
examples.notes: The ROUND() function is used to round a numeric field to the number of decimals specified.

name: CharIndex
description: Returns the position at which toFind occurs within toSearch (starting at position start, if provided) or zero if toFind is not found. Supported since Orion Platform 2018.2 (NPM 12.3) and later.

name: Concat
description: Takes one or more arguments and returns a single string that is the concatenation of the values of the arguments.

examples.query: SELECT Concat ('The ', 'most ','awesome ', 'string') as ConString from Orion.Engines

name: EscapeSWISUriValue
description: Returns a with certain characters escaped. Intended for internal use only.

examples.query: SELECT Uri, EscapeSWISUriValue(Uri) as c FROM Orion.Engines

name: Length
description: Returns the length of string s.

examples.query: SELECT Length(ServerName) as NameLength FROM Orion.Engines

name: Replace
description: Replaces all occurrences of a specified string (pattern) value in expression with another string value (replacement). Supported since Orion Platform 2017.3 (NPM 12.2) and later.

name: SubString
description: Returns a substring of length characters starting at position start (the first character is position 1).

examples.query: SELECT SubString ('123456789', 3, 6) as TestSubString from Orion.Engines

name: ToLower
description: Converts a to all lowercase.

examples.query: SELECT ToLower ('TeStStRiNg') as LowString from Orion.Engines

name: ToString
description: Converts a to a string. In most scenarios this conversion will happen automatically when needed by usage.

examples.query: SELECT ToString(101) as ResultColumn FROM SWISTable

name: ToUpper
description: Converts a to all uppercase.

examples.query: SELECT ToUpper ('TeStStRiNg') as CapString from Orion.Engines

name: UriEquals
description: Returns true if SWIS Uri a refers to the same entity instance as SWIS Uri b.
